_comment: COUPLING tier-2. 'If a coupling converges too slowly to be practical, SWAP WHICH SIDE IS DIRICHLET before doing anything else — that replaces rho by 1/rho and is usually a bigger win than any theta', and the observation that one asymmetric split failed to converge inside the iteration budget with the stiff subdomain on the Dirichlet side and converged comfortably once the roles were swapped. This is the only tuning advice in the knowledge that claims to beat a SEARCH, so the fixture sweeps six thetas in the stiff orientation rather than testing one: a claim that role-swapping beats theta tuning is only tested if theta tuning was attempted and lost. The swapped orientation gets no search at all — just the theta the 1/(1+rho) rule prescribes for the new ratio — and still wins. THE BUDGET IS NOT TUNED: max_iter=60 with tol=1e-8 is the iteration budget in the knowledge's own example couple(...) call, used unchanged, so the fixture cannot be accused of picking the one budget that makes the claim true. The swapped run's physics is checked against the closed form too, so a fast arrival at the wrong fixed point cannot win.
